Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the call earlier — good to align on scope. Quick recap from our side and next steps: 

- Goals: low-latency chat support + transactional summarization for German (DE), French (FR), Spanish (ES) in EU; Japanese (JA) and Korean (KO) in APAC.
- Quality bar: human-like fluency + correct locale-specific entities (IBAN formatting, VAT phrasing, honorifics for JA/KR).

As discussed, please share:
1) recommended model variants for each language/region and expected latency/cost tradeoffs;
2) a small prompt set we can run against our in-house eval harness (we can run locally and send results);
3) any known quality regressions vs. English baseline we should expect.

I attached our privacy questionnaire (PDF) and a sample anonymized transcript.

Thanks,

Hi Elena (and Tomoko),

Great to meet you both — appreciate the clear success criteria. Below is what we'll deliver before the 15 Jun call and a recommended starting config: 

1) Recommended model variants (short):
- EU (DE/FR/ES): Redstone-7B-OPT-q4 (low-cost) for classification/short replies; Redstone-13B-RT for chat where fluency matters.
- APAC (JA/KO): Redstone-13B-RT with locale-specific tokenizer fallback; for highest quality JA please consider Redstone-70B-RT (higher cost).
- Fallback policy: route to larger variant only for >10 tokens or when eval confidence < 0.6.

2) Expected perf/cost (estimates):
- 7B q4: 60-80ms/token on Dedicated A100 equivalent; best for high-throughput flows.
- 13B-RT: 90-150ms/token; balanced quality/latency.
- 70B-RT: 220-350ms/token; highest quality but higher unit cost.

3) Deliverables before next call (we'll share links):
- prompt-set-eu-apac-v1.jsonl (small curated prompts for DE/FR/ES/JA/KO) — attach for your eval harness.
- benchmark links: locale-quality report + baseline English comparison.
- short eval notes on known regressions (e.g., honorific usage in JA; numeric formatting edge cases for IBAN/VAT in some DE test cases).

4) Compliance/security: we've flagged SOC2 evidence and will share a redacted audit pack and the SOC2 PDF for review (we also noted your questionnaire). Neha (cc) will hand this off to security.

Next steps:
- Rishi will upload the prompt set and a quick eval script to the Drive link below.
- Please run the prompt set on your harness and paste a short CSV with accuracy/fluency scores; we'll compare to our internal baseline.
- Confirm the 15 Jun 09:00 CEST slot and whether you want SE + Solutions Engineer on the call.

Elena / Marissa,

Uploading the artifacts now — see Drive link below. Notes from SE perspective: 
- prompt-set-eu-apac-v1.jsonl contains ~60 targeted prompts per locale (mix of transactional, conversational, and entity-heavy examples). File attached as reference.
- Known quality regressions vs English baseline:
  * Japanese: honorific suffix selection (san/sama) in customer responses; we recommend locale-conditioned templates to reduce regression.
  * German: numeric grouping and locale-specific punctuation in currency outputs (we suggest post-processing hooks for IBAN/VAT normalization).
  * Korean: spacing around code-switch tokens; minor tokenization issues with hangul + latin alphanumerics.

- Eval notes: please include both BLEU-style and human fluency judgments; for JA and KO human fluency weighting should be higher.
